simple.meaning: אֲנַחְנוּ (ʼănachnûw) is a Hebrew action word meaning “we.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 121 times in Genesis, Exodus, Numbers, Deuteronomy, Joshua, and 12 more, beginning at Genesis 13:8. The surrounding contexts include family, family line, land.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אֲנַחְנוּ (H587) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: אֲנַחְנוּ (ʼănachnûw) / H587 is traced through Genesis 13:8, Genesis 19:13, Genesis 29:4, Genesis 37:7 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H587. anachnu אֲנַחְנוּ pronoun 1 plural we see below אֲנָ֑חְנוּ אֲנַ֫חְנוּ pronoun 1 plural common we (the plural corresponding to אָנֹכִי , as אֲנוּ ; to אֲנִי ; see W SG p. 100 ; Phoenician אנחן CIS i. 3, 16.17 , Aramaic ᵑ7 אֲנַחְנָא, also נַחְנָא , Syriac , , , ) Gen 13:8 ; 29:4 ; 37:7 ; 42:11 , 13 ; Num 9:7 ; Deut 1:28 , 41 ; Joel 2:17-18 , etc. Like אֲנִי , following a participle as its subject Gen 19:13 ; Num 10:29 ; Judg 19:18 ; 2Kin 18:26 ; appended to a verb for emphasis Judg 9:28 ; 2Kin 10:4 ; Isa 20:6 .
